claim: Capacity Reservations are charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate whether or not you run instances in the reserved capacity; when a matching instance runs, you pay for the instance and nothing for the reservation, with no upfront or additional charges.
question: Do you pay for a Capacity Reservation that you do not use?

values.display: charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate
values.spoken: you pay the On-Demand rate whether you use it or not
a matching running instance covers the reservation

evidence.quote: Capacity Reservations are charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate whether you run instances in reserved capacity or not, including any applicable regional surcharge for Dedicated Instances. If you do not use the reservation, this shows up as unused reservation on your Amazon EC2 bill. When you run an instance that matches the attributes of a reservation, you just pay for the instance and nothing for the reservation. There are no upfront or additional charges.

claim: Billing discounts of Savings Plans and Regional Reserved Instances apply to Capacity Reservations with matching attributes; billing discounts of zonal Reserved Instances do not apply to Capacity Reservations.
question: Which commitment discounts apply to an On-Demand Capacity Reservation?

values.display: Savings Plans and Regional Reserved Instances apply
values.spoken: Savings Plans and regional Reserved Instances discount a Capacity Reservation

values.display: zonal Reserved Instances do not apply
values.spoken: zonal Reserved Instance discounts do not apply

qualifiers.condition: the Capacity Reservation has matching attributes

evidence.quote: Billing discounts for Savings Plans and Regional Reserved Instances apply to Capacity Reservations. AWS automatically applies these discounts to Capacity Reservations that have matching attributes.
Billing discounts for zonal Reserved Instances do not apply to Capacity Reservations.

claim: Capacity Reservations do not ensure that a hibernated instance can resume after you try to start it.
question: Does a Capacity Reservation guarantee that a hibernated instance can resume?

values.spoken: a Capacity Reservation does not guarantee a hibernated instance resumes

values.display: after you try to start it

evidence.quote: Capacity Reservations do not ensure that a hibernated instance can resume after you try to start it.
